$comment: Shared corpus — quilltap-v5 copies this file verbatim and asserts the same outputs. `expect` is the WHOLE match object, or null. Fix the port, not the vectors.

cases.invariant: The ordinary case: a colon after whitespace opens on the second query character.
The closing colon sets `closed` and is NOT part of `end` — the caller deletes it separately.
A colon at the very start of the block needs no preceding character.
An opening bracket counts as word-opening context, like whitespace.
The query is lowercased so the match is deterministic regardless of typing case.
A URL scheme must never open a menu. This is the row that will actually save someone.
A clock time must never open a menu — the colon is preceded by a digit, not a word opening.
A Windows path must never open a menu.
A colon glued to the end of a word is punctuation, not a trigger.
An emoticon must never open a menu. This is why the minimum query length is 2.
A one-character query is inert — it would match half the set.
Space is not in the query alphabet, so `: ` cancels the trigger outright.
A bare closing colon with an empty query commits nothing.
The opening colon alone is inert until two query characters follow.
Empty text is handled without an out-of-range read.
A 32-character query is the longest still accepted (MAX_QUERY_LENGTH boundary).
A 33-character query is abandoned — a runaway trigger from pasted text must not hold a menu open.
